program_name: Biology for One-Health (Bachelor's Degree / Corso di Laurea in "Biology for One-Health"). The programme is officially named in English on all University of Naples Federico II sources; the Italian degree class denomination is "Scienze Biologiche". Both the spellings "Biology for One-Health" (hyphenated, used in the rectoral decree and the Department of Biology pages) and "Biology for one health" (used on the orientamento.unina.it course card) occur on official unina.it pages; the hyphenated form is the one used in the rectoral decree.
teaching_language: English — the programme is taught entirely in English and is part of the University of Naples Federico II "International Catalogue". The orientamento.unina.it course card lists Language: ENG. No Italian-language curriculum exists: this is a standalone English-taught degree (not an English track of an Italian programme). Italian language proficiency is NOT an admission requirement. The study plan reserves 8 CFU for "Further knowledge useful for job placement / further linguistic knowledge", of which foreign students take 4 credits as further linguistic knowledge.
campus: Monte Sant'Angelo — Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo, Via Cinthia, 80126 Napoli (NA), Italy. The programme belongs to the Department of Biology (Dipartimento di Biologia), located in Building 7 (Edificio 7) of the Monte Sant'Angelo complex. The Teaching Office (Ufficio per la Didattica) is at Via Cinthia, Building 7. The student registry office handling enrolment (Segreteria Studenti - Area Didattica Scienze MM.FF.NN.) is at Via Cinthia 4 / via Cupa Nuova Cintia 21, 80126 Napoli, inside the same Monte Sant'Angelo complex. The programme sits under the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (School of Polytechnic and Basic Sciences).
degree_class: L-13 (Scienze Biologiche / Biological Sciences). The 2026/27 rectoral admission decree writes the class as "Classe L - R13 - Scienze Biologiche" (the recoded class designation used after the DM 1649/2023 class reform); the orientamento.unina.it course card shows "Degree class L-13", and the Universitaly pre-enrolment instructions tell non-EU candidates to select "Biology for One-Health" (Classe L13). Duration 3 years, 180 ECTS.
admission_type: Restricted access — "Numero Programmato Locale" (locally capped enrolment), declared as such on the orientamento.unina.it course card. Two entirely separate selection procedures run in parallel: (1) EU citizens (wherever resident) + non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy + holders of an Italian secondary school diploma apply through the Segrepass online platform against a published rectoral call (bando di concorso) and are ranked by an algorithm combining diploma grade and chronological order of application — there is NO competitive entrance exam; (2) non-EU citizens resident abroad do NOT use Segrepass at all: they pre-enrol via the Universitaly portal, are assessed by document review plus a mandatory online admission interview run directly by the Course Coordination Committee (Commissione di Coordinamento Didattico), and are placed on a separate ranking list. In addition, ALL admitted students (both routes) must, as a condition of enrolment, hold a B2 English certificate and sit the mandatory CEnT (CISIA English Test) self-assessment test in TOLC@CASA mode — this test is not used for selection/ranking, only to certify initial preparation and to trigger an OFA (additional learning requirement) when the Mathematics score is low.
academic_requirements:
Bachelor-level entry, so a secondary school leaving qualification is required.

Eligible candidates (Art. 2 of the 2026/27 call, DR/2026/2423):
1) Holders of an Italian upper-secondary school diploma (diploma di scuola secondaria di secondo grado), who must additionally hold an English language certificate of at least B2 level;
2) EU citizens wherever resident, and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy under Art. 39(5) of Legislative Decree 286/1998 as amended by Art. 26 of Law 189/2002, holding a qualification obtained abroad after AT LEAST 12 YEARS of schooling and recognised as equivalent to the Italian upper-secondary diploma;
3) Non-EU citizens resident abroad, under the MUR rules on entry, stay, enrolment of international students and recognition of qualifications valid for A.Y. 2026/27 (published at www.mur.gov.it / https://www.studiare-in-italia.it).

Explicit requirement repeated on the Department of Biology enrolment guides for both EU and non-EU candidates: "At least 12 years of pre-university education (high school diploma)".

Qualification recognition: foreign qualifications must be accompanied by an official Italian translation, legalisation and a Declaration of Value ("dichiarazione di valore in loco") issued by the competent Italian diplomatic/consular representation. Alternatively a CIMEA Statement of Comparability / Statement of Verification is accepted; candidates holding qualifications from the 55 signatory countries of the Lisbon Recognition Convention may use the CIMEA ARDI automatic-recognition tool (https://www.cimea.it/EN/pagina-ardi-automatic-recognition-database-italia).

Subject-knowledge expectations (orientamento.unina.it): admission "requires basic knowledge of the Mathematical, Physical and Natural Sciences and various skills (e.g. problem solving, critical evaluation of data)". Where initial preparation is not verified as adequate, the Course Teaching Coordination Committee (CCD) assigns specific Additional Formative Obligations (OFAs) to be fulfilled within the first year.

OFA rule for 2026/27 (as amended by DR/2026/2551): a CEnT score below 4 in the "Mathematics" section results in admission WITH an OFA; the OFA is cleared by passing the "Biomathematics" exam by 31 March of the year following matriculation (31/03/2028). If the OFA is not cleared, the student is enrolled in Year II but cannot sit any exams until the OFA is extinguished. (An earlier Department notice for A.Y. 2025/26 phrased the threshold as "lower or equal to 4 out of 15 questions in Maths".)

Transfers: students transferring from another Federico II degree programme or from another university must also submit the competition application and be usefully ranked; recognised CFU cannot allow entry to a year beyond the first, because only Year 1 is activated for A.Y. 2026/27.

No prior degree, portfolio, motivation letter or GPA threshold is required. Letters of recommendation are OPTIONAL for non-EU candidates ("optional, but useful for a positive assessment").
language_requirements:
English: a certificate of English language proficiency at AT LEAST B2 level (CEFR) is mandatory for enrolment, for EU/Italian and non-EU candidates alike. It is required for enrolment (immatricolazione), and for non-EU candidates it must also be uploaded at the Universitaly pre-enrolment stage.

Accepted certifying bodies listed by the Department of Biology for both EU and non-EU candidates: Cambridge, BEC, Trinity, IELTS, TOEFL. No numeric minimum scores (e.g. IELTS band, TOEFL score) are published on any official unina.it page for this programme — the attainment of B2 level "will be ascertained by the University Language Centre (www.cla.unina.it) before the enrolment". The CLA (Centro Linguistico di Ateneo) is the body that validates/recognises the certificate.

Official warning in the Department's enrolment guide: "It is worth noting that if individual English proficiency testing is carried out after enrolment, the procedure at Embassy/Consulate for non-EU visas could fail" — i.e. non-EU applicants should have the B2 certificate in hand before the visa stage.

Mandatory CEnT: in addition to the B2 certificate, all candidates must pass the compulsory self-assessment test CEnT (CISIA English Test) delivered by CISIA in TOLC@CASA / TOLC@HOME mode. For A.Y. 2026/2027 the deadline to sit the CEnT is 15 October 2026. Booking link given by the Department: https://www.cisiaonline.it/cent/tutto-sul-CEnT/tutto-sul-CEnT (EN: https://cisiaonline.it/en/cent/all-about-CEnT/all-about-CEnT).

Italian: NOT required. No Italian language certificate or Italian proficiency test is requested for this programme (international.unina.it states that English-taught programmes do not require Italian proficiency).

Students enrolled in a previous cohort were told (Department notice of 30 January 2026, for A.Y. 2025/26): "Students enrolled at Biology for One-Health have to bring the B2 level English certification and TOLC-I English report by the 31th of March 2026" — showing the certificate/test evidence can be produced after matriculation but within a hard deadline.

For reference, the equivalent A.Y. 2025/2026 window was 18 July 2025 09:00 to 29 August 2025 14:00, i.e. the same mid-July to end-August pattern.

required_documents:
A) NON-EU candidates resident abroad — documents to UPLOAD on the Universitaly portal for the pre-acceptance selection:
- Passport
- Updated Curriculum Vitae
- High School Degree Certificate (obtained after at least 12 years of pre-university education)
- Certificate of English language proficiency (at least B2 level)
- Letter/Letters of recommendation (optional, but useful for a positive assessment)
On Universitaly the candidate must also select "University of Naples Federico II", the degree course "Biology for One-Health" (Classe L13), and specify the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested.

B) NON-EU candidates — documents to submit IN PERSON at the Segreteria Studenti (Area Didattica Scienze MM.FF.NN., via Cupa Nuova Cintia 21 / Via Cinthia 4, 80126 Napoli) to complete enrolment (online enrolment is not allowed):
- Passport (to be shown) + one copy left at the student office
- Italian tax code (codice fiscale)
- Proof of payment of tuition fees (e.g. deposit at the bank counter); the guide notes that for these students the fees coincide with the regional tax and the legal stamp, paid only after arriving in Italy
- Passport-size photograph in .jpeg format
- Visa permit (to be shown) + one copy left at the student office
- Copy of the Pre-Acceptance Letter (to be shown) + one copy left at the student office
- Declaration of Value (DoV) OR CIMEA Statement of Comparability / Statement of Verification (ARDI tool usable for Lisbon Convention signatory countries)
- Copy of the English language proficiency certificate
- Report of the CEnT (CISIA English Test)
- Application form

C) EU and Italian candidates — application stage (Segrepass): online user registration (personal data, password, or SPID) then completion and submission of the competition application, declaring the upper-secondary diploma grade (used in the ranking algorithm). No fee, no documents uploaded at this stage beyond the self-declared data.

D) EU and Italian candidates — matriculation stage (Segrepass, then in person):
- Click "Accettazione posto in graduatoria" (acceptance of the ranked place), then "Immatricolazioni ai Corsi di Studio a numero programmato"
- Self-certification of the qualification (autocertificazione del titolo di studio) and of family income data (ISEEU, retrieved automatically from the INPS database)
- Payment of the first instalment and the regional tax (bank transfer and post-office payments are NOT accepted, on pain of exclusion)
- The documentation submitted online must then be PRINTED and delivered to the Segreteria Studenti counters within 15 days of matriculation
- English certificate at B2 level and CEnT report (condition of enrolment; CEnT by 15 October 2026)
- Holders of a foreign qualification: the qualification with official Italian translation, legalisation and Declaration of Value; if course abbreviation is requested, an academic transcript with exams passed plus official documentation of the exam syllabi
- Enrolment for students of foreign citizenship must be done at the Segreteria Studenti counters (the online-only procedure is not available to them).
entry_exam_or_test:
There is NO competitive written entrance examination for the EU/Italian route. Selection is purely by ranking algorithm.

1) SELECTION (EU / Italian / non-EU resident in Italy): ranking is calculated with the algorithm P = 60 (M/100) + 40 ((N-A+1)/N), where M = upper-secondary diploma grade out of 100 (100 cum laude = 101), N = total number of applications received for the programme, A = chronological order of booking/application. In other words: 60% diploma grade, 40% how early the application was submitted. Ties are broken in favour of the younger candidate (Art. 2(9), Law 191/98). The same algorithm is used for the Italian-language Biologia degree.

2) SELECTION (non-EU resident abroad): a MANDATORY ONLINE ADMISSION INTERVIEW, convened by e-mail to the address given on the Universitaly pre-application, "to test the personal preparation about logical ability and basic scientific knowledge" ("per verificare la preparazione personale sulle capacità logiche e sulle conoscenze scientifiche di base"). It is run by the Course Coordination Committee. For A.Y. 2026/27 interviews were held via Google Meet according to a published schedule (notice of 23 June 2026). Document review (passport, CV, high-school certificate, B2 certificate, optional reference letters) precedes the interview. A separate ranking list is produced.

3) MANDATORY SELF-ASSESSMENT TEST FOR ALL ADMITTED STUDENTS: CEnT — CISIA English Test, delivered by CISIA in TOLC@CASA (at-home) mode, after registration on the CISIA portal. It is a condition of matriculation, not a selection instrument. For A.Y. 2026/2027 the deadline to sit the CEnT is 15 October 2026. A CEnT score below 4 in the "Mathematics" section leads to admission with an OFA (Obbligo Formativo Aggiuntivo), cleared by passing the "Biomathematics" exam by 31 March 2028; otherwise the student can enrol in Year II but cannot sit exams until the OFA is cleared.

IMPORTANT NAMING CORRECTION: the original 2026/27 call DR/2026/2423 and the earlier 2025/26 Department notice named this test "TOLC-I_EN". Rectoral decree DR/2026/2551 of 30/06/2026 formally corrected this as a clerical error: the test is the CENT, not the TOLC-I_EN ("è stato, per mero errore materiale, denominato come TOLC-I_EN, anziché come CENT, il test di autovalutazione da sostenere obbligatoriamente per l'immatricolazione, erogato dal CISIA nella modalità TOLC@CASA"). Applicants for 2026/27 must therefore book the CEnT, NOT the English TOLC-I.

No SAT, no portfolio, no motivation letter, no national test (this programme is NOT part of the national numero programmato / semestre filtro system used for Medicine).

Official fees page: https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (English version: https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse). Fee simulator: http://calcolatrice.unina.it. Summary for A.Y. 2026/27 (university-wide, no programme-specific surcharge for Biology for One-Health): the contribution is income- and career-based, calculated on the ISEEU (university ISEE) and the CFU earned. First-year students pay a "reduced contribution": EXEMPT if ISEEU up to EUR 30,000; otherwise a fixed EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component, up to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those who do not file an ISEEU declaration. A 50% reduction applies to first-year bachelor students with a school-leaving grade of 100 cum laude. On top of the university contribution: regional tax for the right to study, in three ISEEU bands — EUR 130.00 (ISEEU up to EUR 25,500, and students from particularly poor countries under Art. 13(5) DPCM 9 April 2001 / D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026); EUR 151.00 (ISEEU between EUR 25,500.01 and EUR 51,000, AND students whose family unit resides abroad); EUR 173.00 (ISEEU above EUR 51,000 and those who file no ISEEU). Stamp duty (imposta di bollo) EUR 16.00. Payment in three instalments: 60% + regional tax + stamp from 16 July 2026 and by 2 November 2026; 20% by 1 March 2027; 20% by 30 April 2027. Students of foreign citizenship must enrol at the Segreteria Studenti counters (not online) and their amounts are differentiated only by citizenship (EU vs non-EU).

[uncertain] The international.unina.it "Admission regulation" page still quotes an older/simplified figure set — "EUR 200/year tuition fees + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp" for European students and "EUR 140/year regional fee + EUR 16.00 legal stamp" for non-European students. These numbers conflict with the 2026/27 official student guide (regional tax 130/151/173 EUR) and appear outdated; the 2026/27 guide and the calculator should be treated as authoritative.

non_eu_reserved_seats: 30 places reserved for non-EU citizens resident abroad ("cittadini extracomunitari residenti all'estero"), leaving 45 places for EU and Italian candidates (plus non-EU candidates legally resident in Italy). The two contingents are assigned through separate procedures and separate ranking lists. Reserved non-EU places that go unfilled are transferred to EU-route candidates usefully ranked; conversely, if the non-EU quota is oversubscribed relative to the EU quota's uptake, eligible EU-route candidates can be recovered in addition to the number stated in Art. 1 of the call.

uncertainty_notes:
1) EU/Italian application closing TIME conflict: the rectoral call DR/2026/2423 (Art. 3) fixes it at 14:00 on 31 August 2026 and its amending decree DR/2026/2551 explicitly left the remaining parts unchanged; the Department of Biology news item announcing the same call says 4:00 p.m. (16:00). The decree is the binding source, so 14:00 is the safe assumption. Applicants should not rely on the extra two hours.

2) Non-EU Universitaly cut-off: the university-wide brochure sets 15 June 2026, but explicitly allows post-deadline pre-enrolment for restricted-access programmes — and this programme is restricted-access. The Department's own second admitted-list window (1-10 September 2026) implies a later non-EU intake exists. No programme-specific non-EU application deadline is published anywhere on unina.it. Prospective non-EU applicants should contact pre-enrolment@unina.it / biologyforonehealth@unina.it to confirm the operative date for their cycle.

3) Test name: 2026/27 sources are inconsistent between "TOLC-I_EN" and "CEnT". The rectification decree DR/2026/2551 settles this — the correct test is the CEnT (CISIA English Test) in TOLC@CASA mode — but the uncorrected name still appears on older Department notices (2 July 2025 notice, 30 January 2026 notice) and in the un-rectified text of the original bando. Data consumers should present CEnT, and flag TOLC-I_EN as a superseded label.

4) Degree class notation: the 2026/27 decree writes "Classe L - R13 - Scienze Biologiche" while orientamento.unina.it shows "L-13" and Universitaly instructions say "Classe L13". These refer to the same class (Biological Sciences); R13 is the post-reform code. No substantive conflict.

5) Campus street number: the orientamento page renders the Department address as "Via Cinthia, 126, Naples, Building 7" (likely a run-together of "Via Cinthia" and postcode "80126"); the bando gives "via Cinthia 4" for the Segreteria Studenti and the non-EU enrolment PDF gives "via Cupa Nuova Cintia, 21 - 80126, Napoli". All three are inside the same Monte Sant'Angelo university complex, so the CAMPUS (Monte Sant'Angelo) is confirmed; only the internal street number varies by office.

6) Tuition figures on international.unina.it (EUR 200 tuition + EUR 140 regional tax) are inconsistent with the 2026/27 student guide (income-based contribution, regional tax 130/151/173 EUR) and appear stale. Use the 2026/27 guide and calcolatrice.unina.it.

7) Data currency: the orientamento.unina.it programme card is explicitly labelled "Aggiornata a.a. 2025/2026" (updated for A.Y. 2025/2026) and its "admission and prerequisites" text still points at the 2025/2026 places and criteria; all A.Y. 2026/2027 figures in this record come from the rectoral decrees of 22 and 30 June 2026 and the Department of Biology news pages (last modified 25/08/2026), retrieved 2026-08-30.

8) A.Y. 2026/27 dates listed here for the EU route (application 16 July - 31 August 2026, ranking by 7 September 2026, matriculation by 15 October 2026) are ALREADY PAST or closing as of the retrieval date 2026-08-30; the equivalent 2027/28 cycle is expected to follow the same pattern (mid-July opening, end-August closing) but has not yet been published.

9) No programme-specific numeric English test thresholds (IELTS band, TOEFL score) are published by unina.it for this programme; only "at least B2" plus a list of accepted certifying bodies. The CLA performs the equivalence assessment case by case.

10) Diploma name vs programme name: the programme name is the same in the degree title ("Biology for One-Health"); the Italian class denomination is "Scienze Biologiche". Graduates qualify to sit the Italian state exam for the Junior section (Section B) of the Professional Register of Biologists under Presidential Decree 328/01.

11) The orientamento.unina.it host presents a TLS chain that some fetchers reject ("unable to verify the first certificate"); the page content was retrieved successfully but the reader should expect occasional certificate warnings on that subdomain.

12) The Department of Biology WordPress site carries injected SEO spam text in its page footers; this was ignored and had no bearing on any extracted fact.
